change.summary: Dedicated-server aircraft use 90 real active seconds per fuel, a shared 16-unit capacity including burning fuel, grounded insertion and configured Y-only ascent.

modifiers.before: Native IA 1.5.0 preloads BOILER buffers up to target 1000 and stochastic per-tick consumption; JEM multiplies grounded consumption by 0.25.
modifiers.after: Server-owned monotonic active-time reservoir; each accepted unit adds exactly 90 seconds only when required by active work. Native presentation receives synchronized utilization/low-fuel state. Offline/unloaded intervals are excluded and remaining nanoseconds persist in entity and packed item NBT.

modifiers.before: Native FuelSlot accepts configured fuel without ground/capacity check; occupied quick-transfer merge bypasses mayPlace. Custom fuel item stacks to 32.
modifiers.after: Custom item stack maximum16. Owner-bound native inventory and fuel slots share a capacity16 including burning units across all boilers. Slot item/no-argument limits also gate occupied merges, drag/hotbar/quick transfer; entity and raw inventory automation admission share the server ground check. Rejected direct writes and legacy overcapacity preserve excess items as nearby drops. Deserialization restores saved items before one-time capacity reconciliation.

after.condition: Powered positive native climb request; airplanes use nose-up vector and do not boost brake input. Only deltaMovement.y changes; descent and horizontal components stay native.

rationale.purpose: Implement master overhaul section1 while preserving native menus, controls, horizontal movement, braking and standalone singleplayer behavior.
rationale.decision_source: User master brief section1, implementation approved without further design confirmation.
rationale.user_requested: 90 active real seconds, capacity16, server-grounded refuelling, saved remainder/readable time, responsive configured vertical acceleration and cap.
rationale.codex_choices: One shared lazily filled reservoir, monotonic nanosecond clock, native slots/inventory extension, actionbar HUD, synced SERVER lift config; old buffer fraction converts against installed configured unit1125, excess old items are returned beside the aircraft without deletion.

introduced.summary: Restore native in-flight engine fuel feeding from onboard inventory while retaining quarter-rate grounded consumption.

history.summary: Restore native in-flight engine fuel feeding from onboard inventory while retaining quarter-rate grounded consumption.

systems: native fuel slots and quick transfer
relations: EngineVehicle -> persisted active-time reservoir -> native synchronized UTILIZATION/LOW_ON_FUEL
VehicleEntity native locally controlled movement -> Y-only configured climb
notes: Installed exact Immersive Aircraft1.5.0 JAR SHA256 7e00754f893d910f301134e0cada37dde0be36c8df15ebf98a5b6512fa664077 inspected with javap and CFR0.152; source bodies are reference evidence, not copied production source.

Five Whys: duration differs by surface -> getFuelConsumption is multiplied onGround -> stochastic per-tick decrement depends on server ticks -> refuel buffers are native integer burn ticks rather than active real duration -> EngineVehicle fuel owner lacked the required monotonic active-work contract.
Configured free fuel/Creative exemption remains native; integrated singleplayer retains native fuel/inventory/motion policy. Registry compatibility retains shared fuel stack maximum16.
No build, tests, static analysis or gameplay launch performed by aircraft worker; root integrates and builds production artifacts.
unresolved: Gameplay acceptance pending: exact wall-clock timing under low TPS, all click/automation routes, reconnect/unload, packed item, controller response and native movement synchronization.
One-tick engine sampling bounds start/stop observation precision; timing is wall-clock based rather than a tick count.
Legacy native buffers do not preserve historical consumed wall time; migration retains their unspent fraction of the current configured1125-unit fuel.
